signs.heading: Early warning signs
signs.intro: Many people have no symptoms. If you notice any of these, schedule a visit and get checked.
items: Numbness or tingling in hands or feet

basics.heading: What type 2 diabetes is
paras: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic condition in which blood sugar stays higher than normal, either because the pancreas makes too little insulin or because the body cannot use its insulin well. It is most common in middle-aged and older adults, but it can appear in teens and young adults too.
Over time, high blood sugar damages nerves and small blood vessels. That can lead to heart disease, nerve damage, vision loss, kidney disease and foot infections that heal poorly.

Risk factors include excess weight, inactivity, high blood pressure, high triglycerides, low HDL (good) cholesterol and a history of heart disease or stroke. Changing these can help prevent type 2 diabetes from developing.

options.name: Nutrition
options.text: A nutrition review and a balanced meal plan, since certain carbohydrates spike blood sugar.

options.name: Exercise
options.text: Activity lowers blood sugar and supports healthy weight, circulation and blood pressure.

options.name: Medication
options.text: Considered when lifestyle changes alone do not control blood sugar.

options.name: Monitoring
options.text: Regular labs and visits to track progress and adjust the plan.

steps.heading: A plan built around you
items: Blood work and an exam, often as part of your annual physical.
Diet, activity and medication if needed, tailored to your life.
Follow-up visits and labs to keep blood sugar in range.

faq: Often, yes. Improving risk factors like weight, activity, blood pressure and cholesterol can prevent or delay it. Screening catches prediabetes early, while it is easiest to reverse.
Not always. Treatment often starts with diet and exercise. Medication is added if those changes do not bring blood sugar under control.
Is diabetes care covered by insurance?
Visits and labs are typically billed to your PPO plan or Medicare. Coverage depends on your plan.
